Am Fluss und an der Bahn: By the river and the railway
Backsteinkirche mit Dachreiter: Brick church with a roof turret
Die Pfarrei wurde 1257 von der Mutterkir: The parish was split from the mother church at Wienhausen in 1257. The old choir carried a stone dated 1338. In 1668 a timber extension was added to the west, and a boarded roof turret, renewed in 1783, with an octagonal slate spire. The restoration of 1994 to 1996 uncovered a painted heaven of angels on the ceiling. The altar is from 1675, the pulpit from 1670, and the organ is a Furtwängler of 1854.
Das barocke Herrenhaus ließ Ernst Wilhel: Ernst Wilhelm von Spörcken had the baroque manor built in 1725: two storeys, eleven bays, timber frame plastered to look like stone, a mansard roof and a turret on the right wing. The von Spörcken family had held the estate since the 14th century. In 1827 the tenant Anton Ludwig Wilhelm Mylius bought it, and the Mylius family still farms it. The park north of the house, along the Franzosengraben, is not open to visitors.
Ein Wohn- und Wirtschaftsgebäude von 161: A house and farm building of 1619, timber-framed, and a listed monument. It is one of the oldest houses still standing in the village.
Fachwerkhaus von 1776, ebenfalls eingetr: A timber-framed house of 1776, also listed, a little further down Hauptstraße.
Das Dorfmuseum in der Hauptstraße 44 sam: The village museum at Hauptstraße 44 keeps what remains of old Langlingen. What is in the cases is something the people here know better than this map.
An der Kirchstraße 1 stehen das Pfarrhau: At Kirchstraße 1 stand the parsonage of 1878 and the barn of about 1880, which is now the parish hall. In the village the group is called allerHaus.
1911 als Wohnung für den Küster und den: Built in 1911 as the home of the sexton and the teacher. A health centre uses it now.
Die Grundschule des Dorfs, Bahnhofstraße: The village primary school, Bahnhofstraße 6. When it was founded, and what colour the front really is, is not written here: the people who went there know.
Die Freiwillige Feuerwehr Langlingen, am: The volunteer fire brigade of Langlingen, on Am Flootgarten. The call-outs that people still talk about are the brigade's story to tell.
Die Aller fließt nördlich am Dorf vorbei: The Aller flows past the north of the village. The first record of Langlingen, in 1257, already names a fishery in the Aller, the visweyde, with a farm of the lords of Meinersen.
Langlingen lag an der Bahn von Gifhorn S: Langlingen stood on the line from Gifhorn town to Celle. Passenger trains stopped in 1981. The embankment is still in the landscape; the trains are not.
1257 steht der Ort zum ersten Mal in ein: The place is first named in a charter of 1257, as Langelege. The lords of Meinersen held a farm here, and the Stegemann farm, together with a fishery in the Aller, as a fief of Brunswick-Lüneburg. The name settled into the form the village uses now.

Ein Dorf an der Aller, Gemeinde im Landk: A village on the Aller, a municipality in the district of Celle, twinned with Czarne in Poland since 1998. End of the tour. What only the people here know is still missing: the festival, the bathing place, the name of the oak.
Eiche, in OpenStreetMap als Naturdenkmal: An oak marked as a natural monument in OpenStreetMap. The map does not say whether this is the old village oak.
